ledger.note: 1500: Cesare Borgia carves out the Duchy of Romagna. 'In 1500 Cesare Borgia, illegitimate son of Pope Alexander VI, carved out for himself an ephemeral Duchy of Romagna' (Romagna page). The Cesare Borgia page has Alexander send him 'to capture Imola and Forlì, ruled by Caterina Sforza' (infobox: lord of both 1499-1503) and the Cesena page says Cesena was 'again seized by Cesare Borgia in 1500' and made capital. The pages name cities, not a boundary.

region.text: Imola, Forlì, Cesena and Rimini, the lands of the duchy in 1500, held under the pope

ledger.note: 1500: the Duchy of Romagna is the pope's creature. Romagna page: 'In 1500 Cesare Borgia, illegitimate son of Pope Alexander VI, carved out for himself an ephemeral Duchy of Romagna'; Duke of Romagna page: the title was created 'by the Apostolic authority of Pope Alexander VI'; Cesare Borgia page: Alexander 'sent him to capture Imola and Forlì'. Mirror of papal-states /ledger/15 (1500 vassal_start): the duchy is tinted as the nearest rule-4 status, a papal vicariate in all but name, while the pope lived. Region: Imola, Forlì and Cesena (the /ledger/0 region) plus Rimini, which the duchy gained the same year (/ledger/1); the papal-states event draws Ravenna, Forlì-Cesena and Rimini provinces, which leaves out Imola (Bologna province) and takes in Ravenna, not Borgia's on these pages. The tint is meant to cover the later gains too (Faenza in 1501, in Ravenna province; Urbino and Camerino in June 1502, which the Urbino dossier tints on its own terms): the duchy is one papal vassal while it grows. Confidence 2: the year is the pages', the status is the researcher's reading (the papal-states dossier says the same of 'the pope is the researcher's reading').
1500: Rimini falls to Cesare. 'Pandolfo Malatesta lost Rimini'; infobox 'Lord of Rimini 1500-1503'. The page gives no day or month; the Malatesta lordship has no dossier.
1501: Faenza surrenders. 'Faenza surrendered'; infobox 'Lord of Faenza 1501-1503'. The page does not name the lord of Faenza or give the date.

May 1501: Cesare Borgia is created Duke of Romagna. 'In May 1501, the latter was created Duke of Romagna'; the Duke of Romagna page says the title was created in 1501 'by the Apostolic authority of Pope Alexander VI'. The state is the one carved out in 1500; same colour.

region.text: Pesaro and Urbino province with Gubbio, as the duchy-of-urbino dossier draws it

ledger.note: June 1502: Cesare takes Urbino. 'In June 1502, he set out for Marche, where he was able to capture Urbino and Camerino by treason.' The Urbino page: 'After the short rule by Cesare Borgia in 1502-03' (reigns table 1502-1503).

June 1502: Cesare takes Camerino (same sentence, 'by treason'). The Urbino page footnote lists him as 'lord of Forlì, Imola, Rimini, Piombino and Camerino'. The lord of Camerino is not named; no dossier.

region.text: the dukedom of Urbino returned to Guidobaldo da Montefeltro

ledger.note: 1503: Urbino returns to its duke. The Urbino page: 'After the short rule by Cesare Borgia in 1502-03', and its reigns table gives Guidobaldo da Montefeltro '1503-1508'. The page does not narrate the return or give a month.

region.text: Faenza and Rimini, occupied by Venice after Alexander VI's death

ledger.note: 1503: Venice takes Faenza and Rimini. Julius II 'set himself the task to expel the Republic of Venice from Faenza, Rimini, and the other towns and fortresses of Italy which it occupied after the death of Pope Alexander'. The year is the researcher's reading of 'after the death of Pope Alexander' (the Cesare Borgia page has the death in 1503); the page gives no date for the occupation. Julius II sent troops against the Venetians in May 1509.

region.text: Imola, Forlì and Cesena, taken by Pope Julius II

ledger.note: 1503: the pope takes the Romagna back. Romagna page: 'his lands were taken from him by Pope Julius II after Alexander VI died' (no year); the Cesare Borgia page names 'the October 1503 papal conclave', gives the end of his lordships of Imola and Forlì as 1503 in its infobox and says his 'lands were retaken by the papacy' (undated). Confidence 2 (it was 1): 1503 is the year the infobox ends his lordships, not a date for the handover of the fortresses, which no page gives. Forlì page: 'a short-lived return of the Ordelaffi' in '1503-1504' before the city became 'more directly subject to the pope than ever before', so Forlì may have passed to the Ordelaffi (no dossier) for a year before the pope; Cesena page: 'Cesena subsequently turned into a secondary city of the Papal States', undated. Imola's own end is on no page opened. Repair 2026-11-01.

ledger.note: 1503: the papal tint ends with the Borgia lands. Romagna page: 'his lands were taken from him by Pope Julius II after Alexander VI died'; the Cesare Borgia page gives the end of every lordship as 1503 in its infobox (Imola and Forlì 1499-1503, Rimini 1500-1503, Faenza 1501-1503, Urbino 1502-1503) but dates neither the pope's death (only 'in 1503') nor the retaking. Mirror of papal-states /ledger/16 (1503 vassal_end, confidence 1). The tint ends here for the lands the pope retook as for those that went to Venice and the Montefeltro (the three losses above).

ledger.note: 1503: the Duchy of Romagna ends with the Borgia. The Cesare Borgia page gives the end of every one of his lordships as 1503 in its infobox ('Lord of Imola 1499-1503', 'Lord of Forlì 1499-1503', 'Lord of Rimini 1500-1503', 'Lord of Faenza 1501-1503', 'Duke of Urbino 1502-1503'), which dates the end of the duchy's lands; the Duke of Romagna page keeps Cesare as titular duke to 1507. Confidence 2 (it was 1): the year is the page's, the hand-over to each successor is my reading (see the three losses above). Repair 2026-11-01.

wars.outcome: Imola and Forlì from 1499, Rimini 1500, Faenza 1501, Urbino and Camerino in June 1502 'by treason'; on 31 December 1502 Cesare 'imprisoned his condottieri in Senigallia'; after Alexander VI's death in 1503 the lands were taken back by the pope, Venice and the Montefeltro.
wars.note: Sides are the researcher's reading of the page: the pope backed his son; Venice was not at war with Cesare on the pages but occupied Faenza and Rimini afterwards (Julius II page). Repair 2026-11-01: the war is clipped to the state's life, which starts in 1500; Cesare's campaign began in 1499 (Cesare Borgia page infobox: 'Lord of Imola 1499-1503', 'Lord of Forlì 1499-1503'), but the page gives no day or month for the taking of Imola and Forlì, so the start of the state is not moved.

notes: No Cliopatria row: every keyframe is new. Start 1500 follows the Romagna page and the papal-states dossier (vassal_start 1500); the title was created in May 1501 (Cesare Borgia page) and the Duke of Romagna page gives tenure 1501-1507, so the 1503 end (bridging, confidence 1) is the loss of the lands, not of the title. The cited papal-states ledger (15, 16) tints Ravenna, Forlì-Cesena and Rimini provinces; Ravenna was not Borgia's on the pages opened (Julius II page: Venice held parts of the Romagna) and Imola, in Bologna province, is missing there. The urbino dossier's 1503 gain from this duchy matches the loss here. Piombino ('Cesare subsequently added the lordship of Piombino to his new lands', siege ended in 1502), Pesaro (Giovanni Sforza 'soon ousted') and Senigallia are Cesare's but no page dates them as part of the duchy, so they are not drawn. Venice's occupation of Faenza and Rimini (1503, then Julius II's 1509 campaign) is the republic-of-venice dossier's to confirm. The Imola, Faenza and Camerino circles are coordinate readings (the gazetteer has none of the three); Camerino, Imola and Faenza are the gazetteer names needed. The seats of the Sforza (Forlì), Malatesta (Rimini) and Manfredi (Faenza) lordships have no dossiers. Repair 2026-11-01: the papal tint is now in the ledger as a vassal_start 1500 / vassal_end 1503 pair (mirror of papal-states /ledger/15 and 16; the note says the tint covers the later gains). The 1503 loss and dissolve are confidence 2 because the Cesare Borgia infobox ends every lordship in 1503; the Forlì page puts a short-lived return of the Ordelaffi in 1503-1504, so the pope may not have been the first taker of Forlì (no Ordelaffi dossier), and no page dates the handover of the fortresses of Imola, Forlì and Cesena. The war starts at 1500 (the campaign began in 1499, no month on any page).
